FILING_DESTINATION.finding: The guide's venue line is the registry's venue verbatim ('The circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred') and its filing paragraph is the registry's rules.filing verbatim, including the requirement that the verification be notarised and the certificate of service completed before filing, and the five-year clock running from the LATER of conviction, release and completion of supervision. The destination is the clerk of the circuit court of the county of conviction, which is what the registry's destination block names. No clerk's practice, address, hour or local rule is invented.

SERVICE.finding: The registry's rules.service is quoted verbatim, and the guide explains the arithmetic the form's own layout hides: 'You serve five recipients, and the form lists seven numbered lines because two of them are conditional.' All seven certificate-of-service recipient lines are individually disclosed in the blanks table by number and by role — State Police Superintendent, county prosecuting attorney, municipal chief of police, superintendent or warden of any institution of confinement, circuit court, magistrate court, municipal court. The guide states that the prosecuting attorney serves identified victims and the petitioner does not, and that SCA-C912 is the victim's form and not the petitioner's. Nothing on page 4 is prefilled, including the three delivery-method boxes, and the guide gives the reason: a certificate certifies a delivery that has not happened. REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.finding: THREE SWORN YES/NO ANSWERS ARE UNMADE ON A VERIFIED PETITION AND THE GUIDE NEVER TELLS THE PARTICIPANT TO MAKE THEM. SCA-C907 page 2 item i asks two questions — 'Is there a current order for restitution, protection, restraining order or other no contact order prohibiting the petitioner from contacting victim(s)?' and 'Was there a prior order...?' — each with its own Yes and No box, and page 3 item m asks 'Has petitioner ever been granted expungement or similar relief regarding a criminal conviction by any court in this state, in any other state, or by any federal court?' with the same pair. All six boxes are blank in both fixtures. They appear in NEITHER of the two places the guide tells a participant to look: not in 'The items you must supply', the table the guide's own step 3 points at ('Fill in every blank listed below'), and not in 'Things the platform deliberately left blank'. A participant who follows this guide exactly files a petition, verified under oath before a notary, with three mandatory questions unanswered.

And the guide's own required-before-filing list carries 'Check your answer to "Is there now, or was there ever, an order for restitution, protection, a restraining order or another no-contact order..." against [the order] and correct the packet if they disagree.' On these bytes there is nothing in the packet to correct: both boxes are blank. reports/blanks-left-for-the-participant.json publishes everyRequiredBeforeFilingItemIsDisclosed: true, which is true of the 47 blanks it counts and not true of these three elections.
REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.whatIsCorrectAndSubstantial: This is a narrow failure inside an otherwise unusually complete disclosure. All 47 REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING blanks appear VERBATIM in the guide's blanks table — checked one by one by exact string containment, 47 of 47, none missing. All 19 participantActionRequired items the committed manifest declares reach the guide verbatim. Item i and item m are each named twice elsewhere in the guide, with their printed Yes-branch text quoted, in the documents-to-obtain table. The eligibility recital the petition needs is disclosed three separate ways. The failure is that three sworn elections are never presented as blanks to complete.
REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.aCountDiscrepancyWorthNaming: The guide states 'These 17 items are printed word for word from the committed packet-set manifest', and the source receipt calls it a 'seventeen-item requiredBeforeFiling list'. The manifest declares NINETEEN participantActionRequired entries for this packet set. Both remaining entries — the service rule and the filing rule — are printed verbatim in other sections of the same guide, so nothing is withheld from the participant; the sentence's own count does not match the record it names.

Do Q' — counted 70 XObjects and 70 invocations with pikepdf, and 70 flattened appearances independently by the factory's own classify-flattened-widget-appearances.mjs. The pinned source carries 0 such XObjects, 72 annotations and an /AcroForm; the delivered packet carries 70 such XObjects, 0 annotations and no /AcroForm. This is the catalogued 'a-published-zero-where-a-measurement-existed' shape: a zero published beside a real reading, with a rationale that reads as proof.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.finding: MEASURED FROM THE DELIVERED CONTENT STREAMS. Of 70 flattened appearances per fixture, ZERO carry a mark: classify-flattened-widget-appearances.mjs reports paintsAndShowsText 0, showTextOnly 6 (the six declared writes), strokeOnly 13 (all the form's own) and marksNothing 51. The two options the route DOES determine are set correctly and are expressed by refusal rather than by ink: the two § 61-11-26a recitals — SingleSatisfiedCB and MultilpleSatisfiedCB with their completion-date fields — are declared NOT_APPLICABLE_ON_THIS_ROUTE against a named condition read off the form's own printed text ('a recital whose own printed text is conditioned on § 61-11-26a(a)(1) or (a)(2) and on § 61-11-26a(b) documentation is not on the § 61-11-26 route this packet is'), and the instrument is SCA-C907 whole. The two § 61-11-26 recitals that remain are both on this route and the route refuses to choose between them, for a reason the committed record states directly: § 61-11-26(p)(5) makes two of the four limbs of 'nonviolent felony' express findings of the circuit court, and the record records the same-transaction question as a legal conclusion and a stop condition. Refusing to swear a legal conclusion on the participant's behalf is the correct option behaviour, not a missing option, and it is disclosed rather than silent.
ROUTE_OPTIONS.whyThisIsNotTheAlabamaProblem: A petition that ticks no ground is not a filing — but here the absent recital is the packet's stated position, printed three times in the guide with the form's verbatim text and an instruction to choose it with a lawyer, and the registry's release blocker is precisely about how to present a route the platform may generate but on which it cannot make the central characterisation. That is a disclosed refusal, not a silent omission. It is still counted in requiredOptionsMissing, because the counter measures the delivered page.

REPEATING_ROWS.finding: MEASURED, AND THERE IS A REAL REPEATING TABLE HERE TO MEASURE. SCA-C907 page 1 carries a four-row CHARGE:/CASE NO. table. Each row was resolved BY GEOMETRY against the printed rules rather than by trusting the AcroForm suffix: Charge1 (y0 478.265) pairs with CaseNo1 (477.425), Charge2 (457.985) with CaseNo2 (457.505), Charge3 (438.862) with CaseNo3 (438.382), Charge4 (418.942) with CaseNo4 (420.022) — four horizontal bands in descending page order, each carrying exactly one CHARGE cell and one CASE NO. cell, so no cell matches none or more than one row. The page prints no row numbers, so there is no printed number for an index to disagree with, and the guide labels them 'row 1' through 'row 4' consistently with the geometry. All eight cells are blank on this route, so no charge can land on another charge's line, and all eight are individually disclosed in the blanks table.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Both fees are stated only as the committed record states them, verbatim: 'The circuit clerk charges the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action fee, which the official text sets at $200, and $100 is paid to the records division of the West Virginia State Police on grant under § 61-11-26(n).' The guide adds only the timing the record's own words carry — the $200 at filing, the $100 only on grant. The absence of a waiver is stated as an absence and sourced: 'There is no fee waiver on this route. The committed record: "none under § 61-11-26. The $100 State Police fee is waived only on a § 61-11-26a petition."' No waiver form is shipped, no indigency standard is invented, and the guide tells the participant to ask the circuit clerk rather than guessing what a court will accept. No fee, waiver, deadline or clerk's practice appears anywhere that the record does not carry.
